id: title:Gilbert09:explain depleted api credits when connecting an x account

review.posthog_relevance: Adds credential-specific error handling and test coverage for the Twitter warehouse connector, distinguishing between account-lookup failures, billing failures, and generic unavailability.
review.reason: P1.F2.H1 implements a substantive, bounded improvement by replacing a generic 500-only status check with specific branches for 402 (CreditsDepleted) and 400, and grouping 429/500. P1.F1.H1 provides the corresponding test coverage. This demonstrates a reliability and diagnostics improvement for warehouse connections without requiring unverified adoption or incident data.
review.uncertainty: The tier relies solely on the implementation and test presence; actual benefit depends on the frequency of these specific HTTP responses in production, which is not established by the code alone.

observations.limitations: This chunk contains two hunks. P1.F1.H1 is a test file; P1.F2.H1 is the implementation. P1.F1.H1 and P1.F2.H1 are not independent; P1.F1.H1 tests the behavior added in P1.F2.H1. No other PRs are present, so no unrelated-PR uncertainty. No tier assignment is requested.

observations.behavior: Adds a 402 status check and a 400 status check, and removes the generic 500-only check; P1.F2.H1 adds a 402 branch and a 429/500 branch, and removes the generic status-code branch.
observations.code_quote: return False, "X couldn't look up that handle. Check the handle and bearer token, then try again."
observations.posthog_connection: This hunk implements the credential validation for the X (Twitter) warehouse connector. It distinguishes between a 402 (credits depleted) and a 400 (invalid request) and a 429/500 (unreachable). This could help PostHog users distinguish between account-lookup failures and billing/availability failures when configuring warehouse connections, rather than receiving a generic HTTP code
